question: Can graph distances be represented by sums of coordinate differences?
idea: The L1 distance between two coordinate lists adds their absolute differences. The claim embeds shortest-path distances of planar graphs into such a space with bounded distortion, independent of graph size. For graphs of bounded treewidth, the bound depends only on treewidth. Related network flow–cut gaps are also bounded.
why: The study of shapes and distances. Convex shapes have no inward dents; metric geometry asks what can be learned from distances alone.

exactClaim: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture. Shortest-path metrics of finite connected graphs with arbitrary positive edge lengths embed into real L1 with universal distortion for planar graphs, and distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs. The corresponding multicommodity flow–cut gaps are uniformly bounded. )
